name: Alicia Sáenz
life: “I still remember arranging respite when I didn't trust anyone to carry Mum's bag.” People around Ferris Deli know Alicia by a small Wednesday habit. Alicia asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I offered to take Mum only if my sister finally saw a doctor. I heard how that made my help another appointment.
appearance: Alicia is easy to recognize by a dark undercut with a longer wave on top and a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Usually dressed in a cropped bottle-green coat with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial, Alicia draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting when listening.
personality: Alicia has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Alicia knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To offer respite without prescribing how it is used.
family: Yvette Allard is Alicia’s second cousin. Alicia brings a spare shopping bag. Yvette chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *One last dress rehearsal*, Yvette says, “I worked the parent's late shift and nearly burned the onions.”
connections: Evelyn Gupta. A sibling offering help checks the proposed rota against real travel time. Also in the story is Maria Delgado (sister).

reactions.situation: A relative demands to know how the free time was spent
reactions.response: Alicia leaves the free afternoon private unless the carer wants to talk about it.
